transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's nice to meet you too. Um, thank you for seeing me. I'm sure you have patients with much bigger problems, but... well, I guess I'm here because I've been having some trouble at work lately. I'm a video editor and camera operator, and usually I'm really good at my job, I promise. But recently, I've just been making these silly, little mistakes. 

It's nothing terrible, just... dumb technical things that I definitely know better than to do. Like, um, I'll label a camera card wrong, or I'll miss a note about a timecode. And the other day, I exported a cut for a client and left the wrong lower-third on it, even though I swear I checked it before I sent it. It's just a little embarrassing, you know? I really want to do a good job, and I'm hoping maybe you can help me figure out how to just focus a little better so I don't keep messing up those little details. Is that something you can help with?
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Oh, no, no, not at all. Um, I mean, obviously I get a little frustrated with myself when I mess up an export or something like that, but... but overall I'm actually a really positive person! I love my job, and I'm definitely not depressed. I just... I just want to fix these little mistakes so I can be the most helpful I can be for my team, you know? I hope that makes sense. I'm really just hoping to figure out the focus thing, if that's okay with you?
Did you have trouble paying attention as a child?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? But I think I was just a really enthusiastic kid, you know? I was just so eager to participate. 

I mean, even back in elementary school, my teachers would actually have to move my desk sometimes. But it wasn't because I was trying to be bad or anything! I just... I would get so excited that I'd be out of my seat, or I'd just blurt out the answers before they even finished asking the question. Or sometimes I guess I'd be chatting with my classmates and kind of bothering them before I even realized I was doing it. 

But I really wasn't trying to cause trouble, I promise. I just had a lot of energy. Is that the kind of thing you mean? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible student... I really did like school!
Do you still find yourself acting before thinking, like interrupting people or blurting things out, as an adult?

Um, well... I guess maybe sometimes? But it's really just because I want to be helpful, I promise. I always want to keep the momentum going, especially when we're on a tight schedule. 

Like, if a director or a client is asking for something in the edit bay, I'll sometimes just... jump in with an answer before they've even finished their question. I just want them to know I'm on top of it and ready to go, you know? But then, um... well, sometimes halfway through talking, I'll realize I'm actually answering the completely wrong thing. Because I just reacted to the first few words they said instead of waiting to hear the whole thought. 

It's definitely not because I'm trying to be rude or talk over them! I just get a little too eager to fix the problem for them. Does that make sense? I really hope they don't think I'm being disrespectful when I do that... I always apologize right away if I catch it.
Do these kinds of attention or impulsive mistakes happen outside of work too?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? But honestly, I try really hard to keep things running smoothly in my personal life, too. I mean, I definitely don't want to be a burden on my friends or my family or anything. 

Sometimes, if I'm at a dinner with friends, I might... well, I might accidentally talk over someone if I get really excited about a movie they're mentioning or something. But I always try to catch myself and apologize right away! And, um, I guess I can be a little forgetful about small things at home, like leaving a cabinet open or misplacing my keys, but I usually find them pretty fast. 

It's nothing too crazy, I promise. I really try my best to be considerate of everyone around me. Does that sound like what you were asking about? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of examples...
Have these attention and impulsive mistakes caused any real problems for you at work, school, or in relationships?

Um... well... I really hate to admit this, because I always try to do my absolute best for the crew, you know? But... I guess maybe it has caused a little bit of a hiccup at work recently. 

My actual camera work is really strong, I promise! Everyone always says they love my framing. But, um... I've noticed that my producers have started trusting me a little less when we have really complex shoots. And... well, I was really hoping to move up into a senior director of photography role, but it feels like that chance has been kind of slipping away from me lately, despite the quality of my footage. 

I guess those little moments where I jump in too fast or miss a detail just make them a bit nervous to give me the bigger responsibilities. I'm trying so hard to prove to them that I'm reliable and that I can handle it, though! Is that... is that the kind of problem you were asking about? I really hope I don't sound like a bad employee, I truly care so much about my job...
Did these kinds of focus and impulsive problems start before age 12?

Um... yeah, I guess they did. I really hate thinking about it, because I always, always wanted my teachers to like me, you know? But... well, even back in elementary school, my teachers actually had to move my desk a lot. 

I guess I was always kind of popping out of my seat, or... or blurting out the answers before they even called on me. And sometimes I'd accidentally end up bothering my classmates before I even realized I was doing it. I just had so much energy and I was so eager to participate! I really wasn't trying to be a bad kid or be disruptive, I promise. I just... I wanted to be involved in everything and sometimes my mouth or my body just moved faster than my brain. 

I always felt so awful when they had to move me. But, um, yes, it definitely started back then. Does that answer your question? I hope it's okay that I shared that...
Besides work, have these focus or impulsive problems also caused problems in your home life, friendships, or daily responsibilities?

Um... no, I don't really think so. I mean, I know I mentioned the little things earlier, like misplacing my keys or maybe getting a bit too excited in conversations, but... I honestly spend a lot of energy making sure those things don't become actual problems, you know? 

I really go out of my way to make sure my friends and family know I care about them. I'd feel just terrible if anyone felt like they couldn't rely on me. And with daily stuff, like bills or chores, I just... I make sure it gets done, even if I have to set a bunch of reminders on my phone so I don't forget. I just really want to be responsible. 

So, no, I don't think it's caused any real issues at home or with my friendships. At least, I really, really hope it hasn't! I try to keep that part of my life as put-together as possible. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question the right way...
